9d984e4a349304d5241f00ef7bea4afe618aac99.summary: Netskope Threat Research Labs reports targeted phishing against banking, finance and government organisations, seen across 42 customer instances. Themed PDF decoys redirected victims through a Google App Engine URL redirect to download a macro-enabled Word document, which then ran a second-stage payload via a native Windows tool. Netskope attributes the activity, with hedges, to the Cobalt Strike threat actor group, which it says has a history of targeting banks and uses Carbanak-style malware. More than 20 other institutions were also targeted worldwide. Netskope reported the abuse to…

subject.name: Targeted Attacks Abusing Google Cloud Platform Open Redirection

hedges: Several decoys were likely related to an infamous threat actor group named Cobalt Strike.
The report expects the group to be actively carrying out attacks, based on the timeline of emails sent to targets.
There is a possibility that the sender email addresses were spoofed with a forged sender.
At the time of analysis, the next stage payload was down and not serving any payload.
The attribution rests on Netskope Threat Intelligence, which the report uses to tie the attacks to the Cobalt Strike group.

9da129c5462b39b82b3ccd2aa70a7e8b3cfe525a.summary: Malpedia family page for NetSupportManager RAT, a modified version of the genuine NetSupport Manager remote-support tool that criminals misuse. The page is mainly a dated list of third-party reports, from 2016 to 2025, on campaigns that deliver it, often through loaders and social engineering such as ClickFix. Named actors are Black Basta, TA571, TA505 and Storm-0506, each as stated by the report that names it. The page gives no CVEs, sectors or countries.
